questions.stem: Amit is 15th from the left end of a row and 12th from the right end. How many people are in the row?

options.option_text: 26 (correct: total = (left position) + (right position) − 1 = 15+12−1=26 ✓)
27 (wrong: 15+12=27 without subtracting 1 for the person himself)
25 (wrong: 15+12−2=25; subtracts twice)
28 (wrong: no basis for 28)

questions.explanation: A is correct. Total people = (position from left) + (position from right) − 1 = 15+12−1 = 26. The −1 avoids counting Amit twice (he is already included in both positions). **Formula:** Total = Left rank + Right rank − 1.

questions.stem: In a class of 40 students, Priya is ranked 11th from the top. What is her rank from the bottom?

options.option_text: 29 (wrong: rank from bottom = 40−11+1=30, not 29)
30 (correct: rank from bottom = total − top rank + 1 = 40−11+1 = 30 ✓)
28 (wrong: 40−11−1=28; incorrect formula)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Rank from bottom = Total − Rank from top + 1 = 40−11+1 = 30. Verify: Top 10 people are ranked above Priya; 29 people are below her; she is 30th from bottom. **Formula:** Bottom rank = N − Top rank + 1.

questions.stem: In a row of students, Rahul is 8th from the front. After 2 students in front of Rahul leave the row, what is Rahul's new position from the front?

options.option_text: 8th (wrong: if 2 students in front leave, his rank decreases by 2)
6th (correct: 2 students ahead leave; Rahul moves up 2 places: 8−2=6th from front ✓)
10th (wrong: that would be if 2 students were added in front)
5th (wrong: 8−3=5; only 2 left, not 3)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Rahul is 8th from front. 2 students in FRONT of him leave → 2 fewer people before him → his position from front becomes 8−2=6th. If students behind him left, his front rank wouldn't change.

questions.stem: Five friends A, B, C, D, and E are ranked based on height. A is taller than B. C is shorter than D. E is taller than D but shorter than A. B is taller than C. Who is the shortest?

options.option_text: B (wrong: B is taller than C, so B is not shortest)
C (correct: ordering: A>E>D>B>C — let's verify: A>B ✓; D>C ✓; E>D but E<A ✓; B>C ✓; C is shortest ✓)
D (wrong: D>C, so D is not shortest)
E (wrong: E>D>C, so E is not shortest)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Build the chain: A>B (given); D>C (given, C shorter than D); A>E>D (given, E taller than D but shorter than A); B>C (given). Full order: A > E > D > B > C. Shortest = C. This type of ranking requires careful chaining of all inequalities.

questions.stem: In a queue, Neha is 7th from the front and 9th from the back. How many people are in the queue?

options.option_text: 15 (correct: total = 7+9−1 = 15 ✓)
16 (wrong: 7+9=16 without subtracting 1)
14 (wrong: 7+9−2=14; subtracts twice)
17 (wrong: no basis)

questions.explanation: A is correct. Total = Front rank + Back rank − 1 = 7+9−1 = 15. Neha is counted once in both positions, so subtract 1. Verify: 6 people before Neha + Neha + 8 people after = 15 total ✓.

questions.stem: Sonu ranks 10th from the top and 30th from the bottom in class. How many students are there in the class?

options.option_text: 38 (wrong: 10+30−2=38; wrong formula)
39 (correct: total = top rank + bottom rank − 1 = 10+30−1 = 39 ✓)
40 (wrong: 10+30=40 without subtracting 1)
41 (wrong: off by 2)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Total = Top rank + Bottom rank − 1 = 10+30−1 = 39. Verify: 9 students above Sonu + Sonu + 29 students below = 39 ✓.

questions.stem: Among P, Q, R, S, T, Q is heavier than P but lighter than R. S is heavier than T but lighter than P. Who is the lightest?

options.option_text: P (wrong: P>S>T, so P is not lightest)
S (wrong: S>T, so S is not lightest)
T (correct: R>Q>P>S>T; T is lightest ✓)
Q (wrong: Q>P>S>T, so Q is not lightest)

questions.explanation: C is correct. From clues: R>Q (Q lighter than R); Q>P (Q heavier than P); P>S (S lighter than P); S>T (S heavier than T). Full chain: R>Q>P>S>T. Lightest = T.

questions.stem: In a row of 50 students, if Kavya interchanges her position with a student who is 10 places ahead of her, Kavya becomes 23rd from the right. What was Kavya's original position from the left?

options.option_text: 18th from left (correct: let Kavya's original position from left=x; after moving 10 places forward: new position from left=x−10; new position from right=50−(x−10)+1=61−x; 61−x=23 → x=38; original was 38th from left; but from right: 50−38+1=13th; new position = 38−10=28th from left; from right: 50−28+1=23 ✓; so original was 38th from left; option text says 18 — checking: if original=18, new=18−10=8th from left; from right=50−8+1=43≠23; so 38 is correct)
28th from left (wrong: if original=28, new=18th from left; from right=50−18+1=33≠23)
38th from left (correct: new position from left = original−10; new from right=23; new from left=50−23+1=28; original=28+10=38 ✓)
33rd from left (wrong: 33−10=23rd from left; from right=50−23+1=28≠23)

questions.explanation: C is correct. Kavya moves 10 places forward (towards left = decreasing left rank). New position from right = 23. New position from left = 50−23+1 = 28th. Kavya moved from original to 28th from left (moved 10 forward). Original = 28+10 = 38th from left. Verify: 38th from left → moves 10 ahead → 28th from left → 50−28+1=23rd from right ✓.

questions.stem: In a row, Mona is 5th from the right. There are 7 students between Mona and Tina. Tina is to the left of Mona. What is Tina's position from the left if the total strength is 20?

options.option_text: 6th from left (wrong: if Tina=6th, students between=positions 7-15=9 students, not 7)
8th from left (correct: Mona=16th from left; 7 between → Tina at 16−(7+1)=8th from left ✓)
10th from left (wrong: if Tina=10th, students between=positions 11-15=5 students, not 7)
12th from left (wrong: if Tina=12th, students between=positions 13-15=3 students, not 7)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Mona = 5th from right = 20−5+1 = 16th from left. 7 students between them, Tina to the left: positions between Tina and Mona = (Mona−1) − Tina = 15 − Tina's position. Setting 15 − Tina = 7 → Tina = 8th from left. Verify: positions between 8th and 16th = positions 9,10,11,12,13,14,15 = 7 students ✓.

questions.stem: Among 6 friends, P>Q>R and S>T>U in terms of marks. R scores more than T. Who scores the least among all?

options.option_text: T (wrong: R>T, but UR; so UT>U; S vs P,Q,R unknown; but since U
U (correct: P>Q>R>T>U and S>T>U; so U<T in both chains; U is the lowest confirmed ✓)
R (wrong: R>T>U, so R is not least)
Cannot be determined (wrong: U is definitely less than R, T, S based on given info)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Given: P>Q>R (chain 1); S>T>U (chain 2); R>T (linking clue). Combined: P>Q>R>T>U and S>T>U. So U is below T in both chains. The lowest confirmed position across all chains is U (we can confirm U < T < R < Q < P and U < T < S). U scores the least among those whose relative order we can determine.
